title: Chapter 179: Main Persona
html:
Breathing became difficult, as though he had entered a bank of dense fog. Moisture clung to his skin, and a red sheen covered everything. Is this the world behind the door?

Remembering Men Nan’s warning, Chen Ge kept his mouth firmly shut. Cleaver and hammer in hand, he surveyed the room. Room 3’s walls, ceiling, and furnishings were identical to those in the real world.

Then he turned around, and his heart began to race. The door stood open, but the corridor beyond bore little resemblance to its real-world counterpart. It was immaculate, free of so much as a scrap of trash.

The mattresses and dolls that had littered the floor were gone; the place looked as though someone cleaned it every day. Chen Ge edged cautiously toward the doorway and extended an arm through it. His limb did not vanish. The door apparently worked in only one direction.

Men Nan had warned him not to speak, so he could not call out to Zhang Ya. Steeling himself, Chen Ge left Room 3 and immediately encountered something in the corridor. It was neither the monster, zombie, nor corpse he had expected, but a doll made from bedsheets and pillows—and it was not alone.

The dolls lined the corridor like scarecrows. Blank smiles had been drawn across their faces, making it impossible to tell whether they were happy or sad. Why do these things exist in the world behind the door?

Chen Ge had assumed the dolls hidden inside the mattresses were part of some sick prank, but this sight changed his mind. Every night, the nurse had given the “patients” their medicine. She had even kept a notebook recording each one’s name and medical history.

Most importantly, every one of those patients was dead in the real world. These dolls probably housed their lingering spirits. A single lingering spirit was far weaker than a Baleful Specter, but ten or more working together might overwhelm one.

As Chen Ge studied them, one doll seemed to sense his presence. Its bowed head snapped up and its body rotated toward him. The face staring back looked as though a child had drawn it, and sweat prickled across Chen Ge’s skin.

The doll stirred, and Chen Ge raised his cleaver. As it drew closer, however, it paid him no attention. It merely tottered past him toward the opposite end of the hall.

It seemed to have no purpose. It wandered the corridor until it tired, then leaned against a wall like an abandoned mannequin. Chen Ge had encountered many lingering spirits, which formed when the dead could not release some powerful obsession and therefore remained in the living world.

The spirit within this doll was different. It seemed either to have lost its memories or silenced its heart entirely. Since it did not attack, Chen Ge had no reason to provoke it. He slipped quietly from Room 3 and examined the corridor walls.

Deep scratches scored the surface, most likely left by Zhang Ya. Chen Ge followed them to the second floor and nearly cried out when he emerged from the stairwell.

Dolls teetered throughout the second-floor corridor. They wandered aimlessly, oblivious to their surroundings. There were far more of them here. Several lay crumpled on the floor, marred by black scratches that proved Zhang Ya had come this way.

Moving among the swaying dolls, Chen Ge felt a strange suspicion that perhaps he was the mad one. Surrounded entirely by lunatics, might the sole sane person begin to doubt himself?

Breathing grew more difficult with every step. A crushing weight settled over him, as though he had been thrown into the ocean and was slowly sinking. Fortunately, nothing attacked. Chen Ge reached the end of the second-floor corridor, where the scratch marks stopped.

A peculiar room waited there. In the real world, Chen Ge had not had time to examine it before the nurse chased him downstairs. The room he had missed was used for electroconvulsive therapy.

What he found inside was not what he expected. The room contained only a single bed, with a boy of about five strapped to it. Chen Ge approached and compared the child with the photograph. There was no doubt: this was Men Nan as a boy.

A question surfaced in Chen Ge’s mind. Why is he here?

The memories buried in Men Nan’s mind suggested a startling possibility. Something had indeed happened to his original personality behind the door, and without its guardian, the door had begun to slip out of control.

Zhang Ya’s scratches ended here, proving that she had visited the room, yet there was no sign of a struggle inside.

Chen Ge had no idea where Zhang Ya had gone, but having found Men Nan’s original personality, he decided to rescue the boy first. Waking him might provide both a better understanding of this world and a new ally.

That was the ideal outcome. No one could know what would truly happen, but Chen Ge had no choice except to gamble. His cleaver sliced easily through the restraints, and he gently nudged Men Nan.

Whether the boy was deeply asleep or unconscious, Chen Ge could not tell. No matter how hard he shook him, the child’s eyes remained closed. Unable to speak in this blood-red world, Chen Ge began considering other ways to wake him.

He did not know what had happened to the boy, so his mind supplied the missing pieces. Whoever imprisoned him had chosen not to kill him. If the child was still useful to his captor, they would not allow him to be harmed.

A reckless idea flashed through Chen Ge’s mind. Silently, he raised the cleaver and tested its weight several times. His eyes narrowed on the space beside the boy’s neck, and he swung the blade down.

The cleaver never reached the bed. When it came within two centimeters, a hairy hand appeared and blocked it. Despite watching intently, Chen Ge had no idea where the limb had come from.

He pulled the weapon back and retreated. Now he could see the monster in full: it had no body, only a severed arm.

The arm appeared to be protecting the boy. To test his theory, Chen Ge struck at him again.

The arm blocked every slash, cracking a little more each time. Just as Chen Ge thought it was about to disintegrate, many more severed arms crawled from beneath the bed.

Their clash grew louder. About ten seconds later, the sleeping boy’s face twitched faintly.
